elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph covers only professional liability (E&O) and cyber/privacy liability; no commercial general liability coverage or per-occurrence limit appears anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No CGL aggregate limit is stated; the insertion contains no general liability covenant at all.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted text sets E&O at 'not less than USD 1,000,000', which is the fallback figure and below the preferred USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted cyber and privacy limit is 'not less than USD 2,000,000', below the preferred USD 5,000,000 threshold applicable to a hosting/MarketSite vendor that processes Customer Data.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation covenant is present in the inserted paragraph or elsewhere in §14.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: No certificate-of-insurance delivery mechanic appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 'Commerce One shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000' — obligation runs against the Vendor/Licensor (Commerce One), at the required amount.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: '...and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000' — express cyber/privacy coverage at the fallback limit.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: both the E&O USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000 limits are stated as affirmative, unconditional Vendor covenants ('shall maintain', 'not less than'), with the obligation correctly directed at Commerce One as Licensor/Vendor rather than at Corio.

Preferred level fails on five of six elements: no CGL per-occurrence or aggregate limits, E&O set at 1M rather than 2M, cyber set at 2M rather than 5M, no workers' compensation covenant, and no certificates-on-request mechanic. To reach preferred the drafter must raise E&O to USD 2,000,000 and cyber to USD 5,000,000 and add CGL 1M/2M, statutory workers' compensation, and a certificate-on-request sentence.

Minimality holds: the drafter omitted the model-language extras that are not in the chosen fallback checklist — 'at its own expense', the 'throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter' survival tail, and the certificates mechanic — and inserted nothing beyond the two selected coverages. No existing words were deleted or paraphrased; §§14.9 and 14.10 are reproduced verbatim.

Intent is preserved: the insertion is a standalone covenant in the miscellaneous section that creates no contradiction with the bankruptcy protection in 14.9 or the entire-agreement clause in 14.10, leaves no undefined term (it uses the defined party name Commerce One) and no dangling cross-reference.

Minor drafting note only (not a defect against the checklist): the inserted paragraph carries the heading 'Insurance.' without a section number and sits between 14.9 and 14.10; renumbering it as 14.10 with consequent renumbering of Complete Understanding, or placing it after 14.10, would tidy the instrument.

Detection status 'missing' is corroborated: the rationale confirms the only pre-existing use of 'insurance' is a net-revenue pricing deduction, so a concise insertion is the appropriate remedy for a hosting/licensing vendor.
